title: Encapsulate public mutable state
why: Publicly writable state lets callers bypass invariants and couples them to representation details.
suggestion: Make the field private and expose behavior or a deliberately constrained immutable view.
limitations: Types explicitly named Mutable followed by a domain type name and configuration models ending in Config, Configuration, Options, or Settings are treated as intentionally mutable containers. JavaScript and TypeScript fields decorated with `@property` or `@state` are treated as framework-managed reactive state.

At most one representative finding is reported per type. Java fields bound by args4j `@Argument` or `@Option` annotations are excluded. Class, enum, record, and struct declarations must begin a source statement; declaration prose, C# expression-bodied properties, events, and operator declarations, plus Dart operator declarations, are excluded. Java and C# fields are reported only when every enclosing type is public. JavaScript and TypeScript modules require directly exported or simple named/CommonJS-exported types. Direct `this` aliases, comma-terminated enum members, reserved expression words, conventional Error contract metadata fields, and instances frozen with `Object.freeze(this)` are excluded. Generic type arguments and factory-call arguments in script class declarations are not treated as class fields. Comment syntax is removed before class-scope tracking.
